chapters.english_title: Who Pays and Who Decides: Outside Pressure
chapters.chinese_title: 谁承担，谁决定：外部压力
chapters.theme: 社会问题、经济与公共生活
english_paragraphs: The outside pressure arrived on a wet afternoon as an advisory letter from the attorney of a private owner, and the effect on the room was immediate. “You may not build a plant on land that is under a legal consideration,” the lawyer wrote. “A vote is not a lawful title.” The judge had already signed the previous order, and the news reached city hall through a message from a concerned voter.

The crime was not the fine itself but the implication behind it. “The offering of a deposit and a clean display of good reputation will not neutralize a charge of bribery,” the attorney said. “A volume of evidence is not the same as a lawful deed, and you cannot legalize an offence with an advertisement.”

“We are not here to grab the land,” Lin said. “We require the room to build what the neighborhood needs and nothing else.” The heir of the estate, a supporter of the resort plan, and an advisory board of two retired engineers all agreed that the attraction would bring a gross profit and a stable base of customers.

The press conference that followed was a strange narration. “They condemn us for racism and surrender to a bull market,” a resident said. “The rebellion of a small neighborhood is not a pretence of rebellion; it is a refusal to confuse a shorts season with a water shortage.”

The gay shopkeeper, the religious author, and the happy volunteer all had a point that the room was missing: the plant would embarrass the town and enable nothing. “The real victim of an illegal pump is a household that cannot appeal,” the author wrote.

The advisory opinion changed the terms. The previous proposal was withdrawn, the deposit was returned, and the group was given thirty days to produce a lawful alternative. “A point is enough to start with,” the attorney said. The reality now was that the plant could not reside on that ground, and nobody could fix it with a win in the press; we would not enjoy the next month, but the law was the law.
chinese_paragraphs: 外部压力在一个潮湿的下午到来，形式是一封来自一位私人业主代理律师的顾问函，而它对房间的影响立竿见影。“你不能在一块处于法律考量之下的土地上建厂，”律师写道，“一次投票不是合法的产权凭证。”法官已经签署了此前那道命令，而消息通过一位忧心选民的信息传到了市厅。
罪行不在于罚款本身，而在于它背后的牵连。“寄存一笔定金和展示一份干净的好名声，并不能使一项行贿指控中和，”代理律师说，“证据的容量不等于一件合法行为，你也无法用一则广告把一桩过错合法化。”
“我们不是来抢地的，”林伟说，“我们需要这块地方来建邻里真正需要的东西，仅此而已。”庄园的继承人、度假方案的一位支持者，以及一个由两位退休工程师组成的顾问委员会，都同意这个景点会带来可观的毛利和稳定的客源。
随后的新闻发布会是一场奇特的叙述。“他们谴责我们种族主义，却向牛市投降，”一位居民说。“一个小社区的造反不是假装的造反；它是拒绝把短裤的季节和缺水的季节混为一谈。”
那位快活的店主、虔诚的作家和快乐的志愿者，都提出了房间里没人想到的一点：这座厂会让镇子难堪，却什么也促成不了。“非法水泵真正的受害者，是那个无从申诉的家庭，”作家写道。
顾问意见改变了条件。此前的提案被撤回，定金被退还，小组获得了三十天时间拿出一份合法的替代方案。“有一个点就够开始了，”代理律师说。眼下的现实是，那座厂不能建在那块地上，而没有人能靠一场新闻上的胜利把它修好；我们不会喜欢下一个月，但法律就是法律。

chapters.english_title: Who Pays and Who Decides: The Decision
chapters.theme: 社会问题、经济与公共生活
english_paragraphs: The decision was taken in a flat above a retail unit, and it answered a simple question: how do we let a building fall into use without selling the land? “The role of the council is to occupy the ground and to halt the sale,” the advocate said. “A cheque and a poster will not rescue a public service.”

The understanding in the room was that the danger was ordinary and the emergency was not. “We have a warning and we have a fire escape; what we do not have is a necessity,” the narrator of the meeting said. “A tale about tradition is not a plan, and a guess is not a production figure.”

The sharp part of the discussion was the refusal of the retailer. “We can forgive a delay and we cannot forgive a betrayal,” Maya wrote. “The innocence of a small shop does not endanger the water supply, and the urgency of the bank does not liberate the council.”

The advocate for the tenants proposed a concerted scheme: a strip of shops on a lease, a flat for the caretaker, and an equivalence between the old rate and the new one. “A reformist measure is worth more than a supposition about the future,” she said.

The vote was seven to five, and the effect was immediate. “We do not immunize a city against scarcity by depressing its rates,” the treasurer said. “We build a habit of paying.” The council would occupy the building within the year, and the sale would halt at the end of the term.

The real issue had been between two ways of holding power: to own or to steward. The activity of the council, its drive to build, and the support of the tenants had produced a decision that neither side could call a victory. Someone had to weave the two plans together, and only then would the order of the day become an act instead of a lie. The advocacy of the tenants was a promise not to betray them, and the building would not sell itself, and the only thing left was the vote.
chinese_paragraphs: 决定是在一家零售店楼上的一间公寓里做出的，它回答了一个简单的问题：我们如何让一栋建筑投入使用而不卖掉土地？“议会的职责是占用这块地并中止出售，”拥护者说，“一张支票和一张海报救不了一项公共服务。”
屋里的共识是：危险是平常的，而紧急状态不是。“我们有警告，也有消防通道；我们没有的是必要性，”会议讲述者说。“一个关于传统的故事不是计划，一个猜测也不是产量数字。”
讨论中最尖锐的部分是零售商的拒绝。“我们可以原谅一次延误，却无法原谅一次背叛，”曼雅写道，“一家小店铺的无辜不会危及供水，而银行的紧迫也不会解放议会。”
租户的拥护者提出了一项商定的方案：一条带租约的商铺、一间给管理员的公寓，以及旧费率与新费率之间的等价。“一项改良主义的措施比一个关于未来的推测更有价值，”她说。
表决结果是七比五，影响立竿见影。“我们无法靠压低费率让一座城市对匮乏免疫，”司库说，“我们建立的是一种付钱的习惯。”议会将在年内占用那栋楼，而出售将在学期末中止。
真正的问题一直介于两种掌权方式之间：拥有，还是照管。议会的那场活动、它建设的动力，以及租户的支持，共同促成了一项双方都无法称之为胜利的决定。总得有人把两套方案编织在一起，只有这样，当日的议程才会变成一项行动，而不是一个谎言。租户的拥护是一份不背叛他们的承诺，而那栋楼不会自己卖掉自己，剩下的只有表决。

chapters.english_title: Who Pays and Who Decides: Consequences
chapters.theme: 社会问题、经济与公共生活
english_paragraphs: The consequences of the decision met the council at a municipal meeting in the town hall, where every section of the public had a view. “This is a political question, not a type of administrative check,” the legislator said. “A certain number of voters will pay, and a common award of praise will not cover it.”

The normal variety of complaints arrived within the week: a protest from the park committee, an enquiry from the retail federation, and a demonstration outside the mall. “We must put the plot apart from the argument,” the mayor said. “A brief in a pocket is not a policy.”

The split in the council was along an unexpected line: the communist member and the fashionable liberal voted together. “Capitalism and communism share one thing,” she said. “Both of them want a compact answer to a complicated question.”

The wedding of two staff members turned into a quiet celebration of the new rule, and a recitation of the old tariff was read aloud as a joke. “A spin of the same wheel will not grant us a conclusion,” the treasurer said. “We must enforce what we execute and execute what we enforce.”

The claw of the prohibition was the deposit. “The wilderness outside the town is not ours to invade,” a resident said, and the similarity between his words and the rebel's brief was remarked on by everyone. “A rebellious tone is not a rebellious deed.”

The social view of the government, the money in the market, and the right of the community to be included: the three of them were now on the same page, and the state had, for the first time, a policy it could start to defend. The government, the community, and the market were included in the same social view, and the law was on the right side. Let us put the money where the policy can start, and let the state show how it works; the public interest was not a normal interest, and the certain thing was that the town would check it. The municipal section of the mall was apart from the rest, and we had to do one specific thing about it.
chinese_paragraphs: 决定的后果在市政厅的一次市政会议上与议会相遇，那里公众的每一个部分都有自己的看法。“这是一个政治问题，不是某种行政检查，”立法委员说，“一定数量的选民将要付钱，而一份普遍的赞扬奖章不能覆盖它。”
正常种类的投诉在一周内到来：公园委员会的抗议、零售业联合会的询问，以及商场外的一场示威游行。“我们必须把这块地和这场争论分开，”市长说，“口袋里的摘要不是政策。”
议会里的分裂沿着一条意外的界线：共产主义成员和时髦的自由派投了同一票。“资本主义和共产主义共享一点，”她说，“两者都想要一个对复杂问题的紧凑答案。”
两位职员的婚礼变成了一场对新规则的安静庆祝，而旧费率的一段背诵被当作笑话朗读出来。“同一个轮子再转一次不会给我们一个结论，”司库说，“我们必须执行我们所施行的，施行我们所执行的。”
禁令的那只爪子是定金。“镇外的荒野不是我们该侵入的，”一位居民说，而他的措辞与那位反叛者的摘要之间的相似性被所有人注意到了。“反叛的语调不是反叛的行为。”
政府的社会视角、市场里的金钱，以及社区被纳入的权利：这三者如今在同一页上，而国家第一次有了一项它能够开始为之辩护的政策。政府、社区和市场都被纳入了同一种社会视角，而法律站在正确的一边。让我们把钱放在政策能够起步的地方，让国家展示它是怎么运作的；公共利益不是一种普通的利益，而确定无疑的是，镇上会核查它。商场里属于市政的那一段与其余部分隔开，而我们必须为此做一件具体的事。

chapters.english_title: Who Pays and Who Decides: The Bridge Forward
chapters.chinese_title: 谁承担，谁决定：通向下一程
chapters.theme: 社会问题、经济与公共生活
english_paragraphs: The ninth arc closed with a public forum in the center of town, where the manner of the meeting was as important as its content. “A logical argument will appear convincing and an authentic one will appear true,” the mayor said. “We must avoid the first and produce the second.” A sorry silence followed.

The interested parties were the postman, a widower, and a resourceful bachelor who had come to advertise a loan scheme. “There is a misunderstanding about what visibility means,” the postman said. “A correct figure that nobody can see is a joke with a tear in it.”

The summit of the evening was the explanatory brief, which was adequate, applicable, and mercifully short. “We can detect the foreseeable error only if we publish it,” the treasurer said. “An exemplary account is one that a disputable line can survive.”

The argumentative member provoked the only real dispute of the night. “A purposeful policy is not the same as a manhood contest,” she said. “An erroneous forecast is harmless if the correction arrives in time. An apologetic one is not.”

The visibility of the accounts, the mercy of a payment plan, and the truthful narration of the failure were the three things the meeting produced. “A satisfactory result would be a boring one,” Maya wrote. “That is what we should aim for.”

The existence of the scheme no longer depended on a single vote. A certain section of the town, a common type of household, and the strong support of the center had built something that could survive a change of council. The next arc would begin with a loan, a summit, and a question about who owns the record. The town, the section, the type, and the term: four words that a strong effect could build into a common center. We must add more to the account and cut less from the record. The political meeting would begin again in the winter, and the certain things would then be the full list and the strong evidence. The build of the scheme mattered more than its size. Aside from the publicity, the fascinating and arguable part was that an observant reader could check every line. They had published who pays; the harder page, who decides, was still blank.
chinese_paragraphs: 第九段弧线以镇中心的一场公开论坛收尾，会上会议的方式与内容同样重要。“合乎逻辑的论证会显得有说服力，而真实的那种会显得真实，”市长说，“我们必须避免前者，产出后者。”随之而来的是一阵遗憾的沉默。
利益相关方是那位邮递员、一位鳏夫，以及一位机智的单身汉，他是来宣传一套贷款方案的。“对可见性有个误解，”邮递员说，“一个没人看得见的正确数字，是一个带泪的笑话。”
当晚的高峰是那份说明性摘要，它充分、可适用，而且幸运地简短。“只有把它公布出来，我们才能发现那个可预见的错误，”司库说，“一份示范性的账目，是那种一条有争议的行目也能挺过去的账目。”
那位好辩的成员挑起了当晚唯一真正的争论。“一项有目的的政策不等于一场男子气概的比赛，”她说，“一个错误的预报如果纠正及时就是无害的。一个忙着道歉的预报不是。”
账目的可见性、还款方案的仁慈，以及对失败如实的叙述，是这次会议产出的三样东西。“一个令人满意的结果会是无聊的，”曼雅写道，“那才是我们该瞄准的。”

这套方案的存在不再取决于一次表决。镇上某个特定的部分、某一类常见的家庭，以及中心地带强有力的支持，已经建起了某种能挺过议会更替的东西。下一段弧线将以一笔贷款、一场峰会，以及一个关于谁拥有记录的问题开始。那个镇、那个区段、那种类型，以及那个期限：四个词，一种强效果可以把它们建成一个共同的中心。我们必须给账目增加更多，而从记录里削减更少。政治会议会在冬天重新开始，而到那时确定的东西会是完整的清单和强有力的证据。这套方案的构建比它的规模更要紧。除了那点宣传之外，迷人的、可争辩的一点是：一位细心的读者能核对每一行。他们已经公布了谁付钱；而更难的那一页——谁来决定——仍然是空白的。
